$description: The Navigator's Source Control panel: what git says about this project, and every verb that answers. It has four moods and the adapter names which one — no project, a first read still in flight, a project git is not tracking yet, and a repository — so nothing here asks whether `status` is null or what `isRepo` means. Under the fourth mood it draws the sync bar (with or without a remote), the branch row, the two sub-tabs, and then either the commit form over the changed files or the log. `panels/git-panel.ts` keeps every decision: what a comparison is, which files group under which component, what a status letter reads aloud, what a commit does before it runs, and which of the four verbs a row's buttons are. Rows arrive as strings and booleans, keyed by path.

style.$description: The sixty-odd `.git-*` rules in `styles/overlays.css`, keyed on `part` and carried here. Four token repairs travel with them, all of the shape `surfaces/panel-imports.json` describes: `--spectrum-font-size-75` and `--spectrum-font-size-50` resolved only inside `<sp-theme>` and a document is mounted outside it, so every rule that read one would silently have taken its px fallback — they are `--jx-text-md` (12px) and `--jx-text-sm` (11px) here, at the same values, and the bare `10px` literals are `--jx-text-xs`. The one deliberate move is the two headline values, the sync label and the branch name: they were 13px, which is not a step on the scale, and they take `--jx-text-lg` (14px). Three rules are DELETED rather than moved, because the kit already draws them: the sub-tab strip's own fill, hover and selected underline are `jx-tabs`/`jx-tab`, the branch picker's box is `jx-select`, and `.git-split-btn`'s hand-built dropdown is the kit menu (see `openCommitMenu`). And one is repaired: a row's action buttons were `opacity: 0` until the ROW was hovered, so tabbing to Stage moved the keyboard onto an invisible control — the reveal is `:focus-within` as well as `:hover`.

& [part=\"empty\"].$description: Drawn here rather than borrowed from `panels/empty-state.ts`, which is a lit template a document cannot call. What is kept is the pattern's rules (§11): one sentence saying what the region is for, then the action that fills it.

& [part=\"branch-icon\"].$description: The hand-drawn 18px branch SVG this panel carried is the kit's `git-branch` glyph — the same key `PanelRecord.icon` already names for this panel's rail button, so the two drawings cannot drift.

& [part=\"count\"].$description: The pill beside a section title. `margin-inline-end: auto` is what pushes the section's own button to the right edge — it was a second rule (`.git-section-header .git-count`) over the same element, and there is only one place a count is drawn.

& [part=\"file-open\"].$description: A REAL button, because it does something. It was a bare span with a cursor and a `title`: not focusable, no role, and Enter did nothing — so the panel's primary verb was mouse-only. A `<button>` needs no role, no tabindex and no key handler of its own, which is three lines of the old row that simply go.

& [part=\"file-actions\"].$description: Revealed on `:focus-within` as well as on the row's hover. Opacity alone hid a control the keyboard could still reach: tabbing through a changed file landed on an invisible Stage button.

& [part=\"badge\"].$description: One letter and a colour, which is why every row's open button carries the status in words as well.

& [part=\"error\"].$description: The wash behind the banner collapses into the page when every author colour is replaced, so the border is what is left to mark it.

children.textContent: Source control keeps every version of a project, so any change can be undone. Open a project to see its history.
This project is not tracked by git yet. Start tracking it to keep a history of every change and to publish it anywhere.

map.$description: One changed file. Every row opens the file it names — renderability decides which VIEW opens, not whether the row responds — and carries the two or three verbs its staged state allows. `$map/item` inside a nested map is the FILE, which is why the row hands its own path back to every action rather than an index.
